title: The Logic of the True Experiment
description: Unlock the gold standard of causal inference: IV manipulation, experimental control, and random assignment vs. random sampling.

slides.title: The Gold Standard of Causality 👑
slides.content:
# The Architecture of a True Experiment

How do psychologists prove that X *causes* Y, rather than merely co-occurring with it? John Stuart Mill established that establishing causality requires three criteria:

1. **Covariation of Cause and Effect**: When X changes, Y changes.
2. **Temporal Precedence**: The cause (X) must occur before the effect (Y).
3. **Elimination of Alternative Explanations (Internal Validity)**: Ruling out all confounding extraneous variables.

A **true experiment** achieves this by combining two indispensable pillars: **deliberate manipulation of an independent variable** and **random assignment of participants to conditions**.

quizData.question: Which of the following is an absolute requirement for establishing that Variable X causes Variable Y?

options.text: Variable X must be demonstrated to occur before Variable Y in time (temporal precedence)
Both variables must be measured using a nominal scale
The correlation coefficient must equal exactly +1.00
The research must be conducted on non-human primates

quizData.explanation: Temporal precedence dictates that the cause must unambiguously precede the effect in time, which experimental manipulation guarantees.

slides.title: Random Sampling vs. Random Assignment ⚖️
slides.content:
## Do Not Confuse These Two Concepts!

Students frequently confuse these two distinct randomized procedures:

| Procedure | Purpose in Research | Primary Validity Supported | Example |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Random Sampling (Selection)** | How participants are chosen *from the population* into the study | **External Validity** (Generalizability to broader population) | Randomly drawing 200 registered voters from a national database. |
| **Random Assignment** | How participants *within the study* are assigned to experimental vs. control groups | **Internal Validity** (Causal Inference) | Flipping a coin to put each participant into the Drug group or Placebo group. |

*Why Random Assignment is Magic*: By assigning participants purely by chance, individual differences (intelligence, motivation, personality, genetics) are distributed evenly across groups, neutralizing them as systematic confounds!

quizData.question: What is the primary scientific purpose of Random Assignment in an experiment?

options.text: To ensure that the sample represents the entire nation demographically
To equalize preexisting participant differences across treatment conditions before the manipulation begins
To reduce the financial cost of recruiting subjects
To guarantee that the null hypothesis is rejected

quizData.explanation: Random assignment ensures that prior differences (e.g., baseline anxiety, intelligence) are balanced equally across conditions, preserving internal validity.

slides.title: Psychology Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
### The Power of the Control Group

A true experiment must include an adequate comparison condition. If you test a new therapy on 50 depressed patients and 40 improve, you cannot claim the therapy worked unless you compare them to a matched control group that did not receive the therapy (to rule out spontaneous remission and placebo effects)!
